decisions.title: AES-256-GCM cryptographic profile
decisions.issue: GCM permits several supported tag lengths and IV constructions while this package needs one stable profile.
interpretations: Permit every GCM parameter allowed by the recommendation.
Fix a 256-bit AES key, 96-bit nonce, and 128-bit authentication tag.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained-peer comparison is recorded; Go crypto/cipher is the implementation boundary.
decisions.selected_behavior: Use AES with a 256-bit key in GCM with a fresh 96-bit nonce and a 128-bit authentication tag.
decisions.rationale: One fixed profile removes parameter negotiation from persisted envelopes and provider-private wrapped keys.
decisions.security_consequences: Nonce uniqueness remains mandatory for each key and authentication failures are terminal.
decisions.resource_consequences: Each ciphertext carries a 12-byte nonce and 16-byte tag.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Changing the key, nonce, or tag sizes requires a new versioned format.
decisions.wire_consequences: The primitive profile constrains fields inside repository-owned formats but does not standardize those formats.
decisions.upstream_status: No upstream issue exists; the external algorithms are used without modification.
decisions.reconsider_when: NIST SP 800-38D or FIPS 197 is revised, or the Go standard library changes its GCM contract.

decisions.title: Envelope version 1 binary framing
decisions.section: Repository-owned envelope policy; NIST SP 800-38D does not define application framing
decisions.issue: The cryptographic recommendation defines GCM inputs and outputs but no persistence envelope.
interpretations: Persist provider output and ciphertext as separate application fields.
Use one bounded versioned binary envelope owned by this repository.
decisions.peer_behavior: No peer format is claimed because SEV1 is private to this package.
decisions.selected_behavior: Encode magic SEV1, version 1, algorithm 1, big-endian lengths, key reference, wrapped key, 12-byte nonce, ciphertext, and 16-byte tag.
decisions.rationale: A self-describing bounded format preserves stable persistence and permits future version dispatch.
decisions.security_consequences: The parser authenticates payload data only after structural validation and rejects unknown algorithms and versions.
decisions.resource_consequences: Length fields and package maxima bound allocation before cryptographic processing.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Version 1 bytes remain stable; incompatible framing requires a new version.
decisions.wire_consequences: SEV1 is repository-owned wire policy and is not represented as an externally standardized envelope.
decisions.upstream_status: Not applicable; this repository owns the format.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new envelope version or algorithm identifier is proposed.

decisions.title: Canonical encryption-context AAD encoding
decisions.section: Section 5.2.1.1 defines AAD input but not application map serialization
decisions.issue: GCM accepts an AAD string but does not define how an unordered application map becomes that string.
interpretations: Use caller map iteration order.
Sort keys and encode every key and value with an unsigned 32-bit big-endian length prefix.
decisions.peer_behavior: No peer encoding is applicable because the context serialization is package-owned.
decisions.selected_behavior: Sort context keys lexicographically and encode each key and value as a uint32 big-endian length followed by exact bytes.
decisions.rationale: Canonical bytes make encryption and decryption independent of Go map iteration order.
decisions.security_consequences: Exact context changes fail GCM authentication and keyring wrapping authentication.
decisions.resource_consequences: Context entry, key, value, and total encoded sizes are bounded before allocation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Changing serialization would make persisted envelopes undecryptable without a new version.
decisions.wire_consequences: The canonical byte encoding is repository-owned authenticated application data, not an external wire standard.
decisions.upstream_status: Not applicable; this repository owns the encoding.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new context encoding version or cross-language package contract is proposed.

decisions.title: Strict parsing and bounded envelope inputs
decisions.section: Repository-owned parser policy outside the GCM primitive contract
decisions.issue: The cryptographic recommendation does not define safe parsing limits for an application envelope.
interpretations: Let downstream allocation or GCM reject malformed values.
Reject malformed, oversized, non-canonical, or trailing input before decryption.
decisions.peer_behavior: No peer parser comparison is recorded for the private SEV1 format.
decisions.selected_behavior: Reject wrong magic, version, algorithm, nonce size, inconsistent lengths, oversized fields, truncation, and trailing bytes; bound plaintext to 4 MiB.
decisions.rationale: Early structural validation makes allocation and error behavior deterministic for untrusted persisted bytes.
decisions.security_consequences: Malformed input cannot select algorithms or bypass authenticated parsing.
decisions.resource_consequences: Declared limits bound all field copies and complete envelope allocation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Previously invalid encodings remain rejected; expanding a bound requires explicit review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Only canonical version 1 encodings are accepted.
decisions.upstream_status: Not applicable; this repository owns parser limits.
decisions.reconsider_when: Persistence requirements exceed a current bound or a new envelope version is introduced.

decisions.title: Keyring wrapped-key version 1 format
decisions.section: Repository-owned keyring provider policy; NIST SP 800-38D defines GCM but not wrapped-key framing
decisions.issue: GCM does not define a provider-private wrapped-data-key record or application key-reference binding.
interpretations: Return raw GCM output with implicit parameters.
Prefix a version and nonce, and authenticate the key reference plus canonical context.
decisions.peer_behavior: No peer format is claimed because the keyring bytes are private to this provider adapter.
decisions.selected_behavior: Encode version 1, a 12-byte nonce, a 32-byte encrypted data key, and a 16-byte tag; AAD is the uint32 big-endian key-reference length, exact key reference, and canonical context.
decisions.rationale: Versioned provider-private bytes keep rotation references and authenticated context explicit without exposing the wrapping key.
decisions.security_consequences: A changed reference, context, nonce, ciphertext, or tag fails authentication.
decisions.resource_consequences: The fixed wrapped-key size and bounded reference/context prevent unbounded allocation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Existing version 1 wrapped keys remain decryptable while their key reference remains in the immutable keyring.
decisions.wire_consequences: The wrapped-key representation is provider-private repository policy, nested inside SEV1, and not an external key-wrap format.
decisions.upstream_status: Not applicable; this repository owns the provider-private format.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new wrapping algorithm, key size, or provider-private format version is proposed.

decisions.title: Fresh randomness and plaintext data-key lifetime
decisions.section: Section 8 nonce uniqueness requirement; plaintext-memory cleanup is repository policy
decisions.issue: GCM requires IV uniqueness but does not define application data-key reuse or Go memory cleanup semantics.
interpretations: Reuse data keys or derive nonces from application state.
Generate one-use data keys and random nonces, then best-effort overwrite plaintext key copies.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained-peer memory-zeroization comparison is recorded.
decisions.selected_behavior: Request or generate a fresh 32-byte data key per payload, read each 12-byte nonce from crypto/rand, and best-effort zero plaintext data-key slices after use.
decisions.rationale: One-use keys and random nonces avoid package-managed counters; zeroization narrows ordinary plaintext key lifetime within Go's runtime limits.
decisions.security_consequences: Entropy failure aborts encryption and zeroization is not claimed as a compiler- or runtime-enforced erasure guarantee.
decisions.resource_consequences: Each operation performs bounded entropy reads and one bounded overwrite.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers cannot request nonce or data-key reuse through the public API.
decisions.wire_consequences: Fresh nonce bytes vary every encryption while the format remains unchanged.
decisions.upstream_status: No upstream issue exists; best-effort zeroization is explicitly bounded to application-owned slices.
decisions.reconsider_when: The runtime provides stronger secret-memory primitives or the nonce-generation policy changes.

decisions.title: AWS KMS AES-256 data-key request policy
decisions.specification: AWS KMS SDK Go v2 service/kms v1.55.0
decisions.section: GenerateDataKeyInput KeySpec and EncryptionContext; DecryptInput EncryptionAlgorithm, EncryptionContext, and KeyId
decisions.issue: AWS KMS exposes multiple data-key sizes and decrypt request modes while the envelope profile supports only AES-256-GCM.
interpretations: Permit caller-selected KMS data-key and decrypt algorithms.
Fix GenerateDataKey to AES_256 and Decrypt to SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT with exact key and context binding.
decisions.peer_behavior: Recording-client tests use official SDK v1.55.0 request and response types; no live AWS provider execution is claimed.
decisions.selected_behavior: Send KeySpec AES_256 and the exact encryption context to GenerateDataKey; send SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT, the exact key reference, ciphertext, and context to Decrypt.
decisions.rationale: A fixed provider request matches the package's 32-byte data-key contract and preserves exact authentication context.
decisions.security_consequences: The adapter rejects malformed outputs and never falls back to implicit algorithm selection.
decisions.resource_consequences: Provider responses are copied only after fixed-size and bounded validation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Keys and policies must allow GenerateDataKey and Decrypt for the selected symmetric KMS key.
decisions.wire_consequences: AWS CiphertextBlob remains opaque inside the repository-owned envelope.
decisions.upstream_status: No upstream issue exists; the adapter selects supported AWS KMS request values.
decisions.reconsider_when: The pinned AWS KMS SDK model changes these fields or the package adopts another data-key algorithm.

decisions.title: AWS KMS resolved-key identity persistence and validation
decisions.specification: AWS KMS SDK Go v2 service/kms v1.55.0
decisions.section: DecryptOutput KeyId and EncryptionAlgorithm response fields
decisions.issue: AWS KMS resolves aliases during data-key generation, so the application must decide which identity to persist and require during decryption.
interpretations: Persist the caller's alias and trust later successful responses.
Persist the resolved GenerateDataKey KeyId and require Decrypt to return that exact identity and algorithm.
decisions.peer_behavior: Official SDK response types expose the identity and algorithm; no live alias-rotation behavior is claimed.
decisions.selected_behavior: Persist the valid nonempty KeyId returned by GenerateDataKey, then accept Decrypt output only when its KeyId equals that persisted reference and its algorithm is SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT.
decisions.rationale: Resolving an alias once makes each envelope retain the concrete key identity while exact decrypt validation prevents later alias retargeting from changing that envelope's key contract.
decisions.security_consequences: New writes may follow an alias at generation time, while existing envelopes remain bound to their persisted resolved identity and mismatched decrypt responses fail closed.
decisions.resource_consequences: Identity comparison is bounded by the existing key-reference limit.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers may use an alias for new writes, but must retain permission to decrypt with every resolved key identity persisted by existing envelopes.
decisions.wire_consequences: SEV1 persists the GenerateDataKey response KeyId rather than the caller's possibly mutable alias.
decisions.upstream_status: No upstream issue exists; this is an intentional stricter application policy over provider responses.
decisions.reconsider_when: AWS KMS changes alias resolution or response identity semantics.

decisions.title: AWS KMS verify-only raw-message algorithm allowlist
decisions.specification: AWS KMS SDK Go v2 service/kms v1.55.0
decisions.section: VerifyInput MessageType and SigningAlgorithm; repository-owned reviewed allowlist
decisions.issue: AWS KMS exposes signing algorithms and message modes beyond the verify-only raw-statement profile supported here.
interpretations: Expose every provider enum and implicit mode.
Require RAW and explicitly allow only PSS SHA-2, ECDSA SHA-2, and Ed25519 SHA-512 variants.
decisions.peer_behavior: Recording-client tests prove the pinned SDK seam only; they do not prove live AWS KMS or independent signature implementation agreement.
decisions.selected_behavior: Verify only RAW messages with RSASSA_PSS_SHA_256, RSASSA_PSS_SHA_384, RSASSA_PSS_SHA_512, ECDSA_SHA_256, ECDSA_SHA_384, ECDSA_SHA_512, or ED25519_SHA_512; reject PKCS1 v1.5, DIGEST, SM2, ML_DSA, and implicit algorithms.
decisions.rationale: An explicit allowlist prevents provider model growth from silently expanding the package's accepted authentication policy.
decisions.security_consequences: The boundary cannot sign and rejects unreviewed or legacy signature choices before provider I/O.
decisions.resource_consequences: Raw messages remain bounded to the AWS KMS raw-message limit.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers must choose one reviewed algorithm matching the asymmetric KMS key specification.
decisions.wire_consequences: No signature wire format is defined; exact message and signature bytes are forwarded to AWS KMS.
decisions.upstream_status: No upstream issue exists; the package intentionally supports a strict subset of provider algorithms.
decisions.reconsider_when: AWS KMS changes its model or another signature algorithm is proposed with attributable standards review.

decisions.title: AWS KMS verification bounds and response matching
decisions.specification: AWS KMS SDK Go v2 service/kms v1.55.0
decisions.section: VerifyInput RAW message size and VerifyOutput KeyId, SigningAlgorithm, and SignatureValid fields
decisions.issue: Provider request limits are documented, but application failure classification and exact response matching remain caller policy.
interpretations: Treat any successful response as verification.
Bound inputs and require SignatureValid plus exact returned key and algorithm.
decisions.peer_behavior: Official SDK types and a recording client exercise request and response handling without claiming a live-provider test.
decisions.selected_behavior: Reject empty or over-4096-byte raw messages and invalid inputs; require SignatureValid true and exact response KeyId and SigningAlgorithm; return typed redacted failures.
decisions.rationale: Local bounds avoid avoidable provider calls and exact response matching keeps authentication tied to the requested statement contract.
decisions.security_consequences: False, malformed, mismatched, or failed provider responses cannot authenticate a statement, and rendered errors omit provider causes.
decisions.resource_consequences: Message, key reference, and signature copies are bounded before provider invocation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers receive stable error classification rather than provider-specific rendered errors.
decisions.wire_consequences: The verifier persists no wire representation and forwards exact bounded byte slices.
decisions.upstream_status: No upstream issue exists; response matching and redaction are repository-owned defensive policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: AWS KMS changes RAW message bounds or response fields.
